title: Canto 4: The Creation of the Fourth Order, the Lord's Protection - Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 4
content:
Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 4

4.1

Title: The first picture is a painting titled ‘Manu’

Artist: © of Wim Kuenen. (Prema, used with permission).

Source: Prema.exto.nl

4.2

Title: The Hindu vintage image shows Śiva as the one loved by all during his marriage.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

4.3

Title: Satī desirous of visiting her family.

Artist: © Vlad Holst, used with permission

Source: Ten Dreams.org

4.4

Title: ‘A woman goes Sati’.

Artist: Nandalal Bose 1943.

Source: wikipedia.org & National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi, Acc. no. 4797.

4.5

Title: ‘Śiva carrying Satī on his trident’. India, Himachal Pradesh, Kangra, ca. 1800.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), collectionsonline.lacma.org

4.6

Title: The first picture is a coloured aquatint titled:’The Entrance to Kailasa’.

Artist/Engraver: Daniell, Thomas (1749-1840). Date: 1803.

Source: wikipedia.org & British Library Online Gallery

4.7

Title: The painting is an instructional plate representative of the Supreme Personality restoring Dakṣa’s consciousness combined with scenes of what preceded the event.

Artist: Hindu artist unknown.

Source: Unknown. The text was digitally removed.

4.8

Title: Dhruva.

Artist: Asit Kumar Haldar.

Source: ‘Myths of the Hindus and Buddhists’, Ballantine Press, Oct. 1913.

4.9

Title: Dhruva before Viṣṇu.

Artist: Dominique Amendola. Used with permission.

Source: dominiqueamendola.com

4.10

Title: A guarding Yakṣa, at the entrance of the Grand Palais in Bangkok, Thailand.

Artist: Photo by tourist.

Source: Wikimedia.org

4.11

Title: ‘Kṛṣṇa Dancing with Gopis in Vṛndāvana’.

Artist: Unknown. Folio from a Balagopalastuti (Praise for the young Lord of the Cowherds), India, Gujarat, South Asia ca. 1450-1475.

Source/Courtesy: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), collections.lacma.org​

4.12

The picture is a digitally produced collage by Anand Aadhar of a popular vintage picture of Kṛṣṇa and two classical western paintings titled:

Title: ‘The Voyage of Life Youth’ by Thomas Cole (1801-1848).

Source: National Gallery of Art

The picture is placed against the backdrop of the mountains of ‘Der Watzmann’ by:

Artist: Caspar David Friedrich 1824-1825.

Source: Wikimedia.org

4.13

Title: ‘Jacob’s Ladder’.

Artist: William Blake.

Source: British Museum, britishmuseum.org

4.14

Title: ‘Good and Evil’.

Artist: William Blake.

Source: William Blake Archive, blakearchive.org

4.15

Title: ‘The Four-Headed Brahmā Instructs Pṛthu’.

Artist: © Johannes Ptok (Aka Janmanalaya)

Source: Consciousart gallery & Ptok.se

4.16

Title: The Hindu vintage image is a representation of Lord Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī as the divine couple to rule the world.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

4.17

Title: 'Pṛthu chases the goddess earth’,

from an illustrated manuscript of the Bhagavata Puraṇa Indian, Pahari, about 1740

Artist / Attributed to: Manaku, Indian, about 1700–1760.

Source: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, & Wikimedia.org

4.18

Title: The classical painting shows Kṛṣṇa and His cows.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet.

4.19

Title: The classical picture shows Kṛṣṇa tending the horses.

Artist: Unknown

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com

4.20

Title: The painting shows a Vaiṣṇava guru/disciple association.

Artist: Unknown

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com

4.21

Title: The classical painting shows an association of monks at the feet of a guru of instruction.

Artist: Unknown

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com

4.22

Title: The painting shows Valmiki discussing with disciples in his ashram.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

4.23

Title: The picture shows a yogi meditating to leave his body.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

4.24

Title: The painting is a vintage Hindu image of a loving Śiva.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

4.25

Title: The painting is titled ‘Young Woman’.

Artist: Raja Ravi Varma

Source: Wikipedia.org

4.26

Title: The picture is titled: ‘Boar Hunt’.

Artist: Kailash Raj.

Source: © Exotic India Art, exoticindiaart.com. Used with permission.

4.27

Title: The Mughal painting with an expounding Nārada is titled ‘Kedar Ragini’. It is from the

Chunar Ragamala. Shaykh Hatim, Indian, Hara dynasty 1591.

Artist: Unknown

Source/Courtesy: Smithsonian Freer Sackler Gallery

4.28

Title: ‘The Lover’s Whirlwind’. It illustrates Hell in Canto V of Dante’s Inferno, 1824.

Artist: William Blake

Source: City Museum and Art Gallery, Birmingham (Museum) & wikipedia.org

4.29

Title: ‘Reïncarnatie’.

Artist: © Wim Kuenen (Prema, used with permission).

Source: Prema.exto.nl

4.30

Title: The contemporary Hindu-image of Viṣṇu is part of a personal collection.

Artist: Unknown

Source: saranaagathi.files.wordpress.com

4.31

Title: The painting shows Nārada preaching before the Pracetās.

Artist: Unknown

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com
